scenes.title: The City That Codes
scenes.tagline: how Bengaluru became India's technology capital
scenes.narration: Every day, a million engineers in one Indian city write code the whole world runs on.
It started in 1985, on Miller's Road, with a satellite dish.

lines: The dish that linked India to the world
scenes.narration: Texas Instruments was setting up the first multinational design centre in India. The dish that linked it to America arrived on a bullock cart.
Back then, Bangalore was a quiet city of gardens. People called it a pensioners' paradise.

scenes.title: How a quiet city changed

events.label: Texas Instruments opens India's first multinational R&D centre

scenes.narration: Infosys had already moved here in 1983. Texas Instruments followed. Forty years later, the city's tech workforce crossed one million.

scenes.label: tech workers in ==Bengaluru==
scenes.narration: Over one million tech workers. One of the largest tech talent pools in Asia.

scenes.title: Glass towers where the fields used to be.
scenes.narration: Tech parks rose across Whitefield, Electronic City and Manyata, glass towers where the fields used to be.

scenes.title: of India's software & services exports
scenes.label: come from Karnataka, almost all of it from Bengaluru
scenes.narration: Today, Karnataka produces forty one percent of India's software and services exports, and nearly all of it comes from Bengaluru.

scenes.title: Written in Bengaluru. Used everywhere.
scenes.source: RBI: US & Canada are the top destination for India's software exports
scenes.narration: Most of that software flows to America and Europe, into the apps, banks and airlines people use every day.

scenes.headline: The city that codes the world.
scenes.narration: From a bullock cart to a million engineers. Bengaluru, the city that codes the world.
